content.comment_body: I'm wondering if it's possible to connect a PT1000 sensor to an [product_name] module designed for PT100 sensors? Regards, [user_name]
Hello, As far as I know, the [product_name] module is only compatible with PT100 sensors. Regards, [user_name]

Hello! I agree with [user_name]... A PT100 sensor has a resistance of 100 ohms at 0ºC, while a PT1000 has 1000 ohms at 0ºC. [product_name] modules aren't designed for the higher resistance of PT1000 sensors.

Hi, To connect a PT1000 sensor, you'll need a transformer. At [url], I found a flexible device called "MU-P" which supports both PT100 and PT1000 sensors and offers various measurement ranges. It outputs 4–20mA and 0–10V, making it adaptable, and it can provide higher resolution than the [product_name] module depending on your temperature range. The price for two MU-P units is comparable to one [product_name] module. Hope this helps! Best regards, [user_name]
Thank you for all the advice.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discuss that the [product_name] module is limited to PT100 sensors and does not directly support PT1000 sensors due to differing resistances. An alternative approach is suggested using an external transformer device, which enables PT1000 sensor compatibility and broader measurement options. The conversation highlights current limitations in module flexibility and suggests third-party solutions for expanding usage scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] module to have support for both PT100 and PT1000 sensors or to offer straightforward methods for connecting PT1000 sensors.
